description: "Join my crew to build AI that predicts fire in zero gravity—where elite Data Engineering meets the final frontier."
summary:
Here is the summary in exactly one single paragraph:

This project addresses the challenge of translating raw NASA NISAR Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) data into human-readable scientific reports to monitor floods, earthquakes, and volcanoes across Africa. Because SAR data is a complex matrix of electromagnetic echoes, we built an Explainable AI pipeline that extracts physical metrics (HH backscatter, Texture Variance, and Radar Vegetation Index) and tested two distinct approaches. Our first approach, a Rule-Based Physics Expert System, was highly transparent but too rigid for complex terrains. Our second approach, a Neurosymbolic Machine Learning pipeline using Contrastive Learning and a Random Forest, achieved 90% confidence on clear volcanic and flood signatures but exposed the "Radar Ambiguity Problem" and "Domain Shift" on unseen data, where the lack of macro-spatial context caused it to confuse vegetated fault lines with volcanoes. Finally, a Vision-Language Model (Qwen2-VL) translates these AI predictions and hard physics into clear text. Ultimately, this prototype proves that while local physics and ML are foundational for radar translation, future iterations must integrate deep U-Net CNNs to capture global macro-geometry and distinguish the circular shape of volcanoes from the linear fractures of tectonic faults.
